subject: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hernandez <tom@shoply.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@shoply.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Tom / Priya,

Thanks again for taking time today - great conversation. Below is a short recap to make sure we're aligned on pain, goals, and next steps. Please tell me if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points
- Cost: OpenAI / Anthropic spend has increased significantly as usage scaled (you mentioned spikes during promotions).
- Latency variability: some inference endpoints see p95 latency spikes impacting UX during peak loads.
- Vendor lock-in: heavy reliance on proprietary APIs makes A/B testing alternate models and controlling unit economics hard.
- Ops complexity: differing feature parity (function calling, streaming, role-based outputs) across providers.

Current stack / usage (what I heard)
- Primary: OpenAI (chat/generation) + Anthropic for assistant flows.
- Volume: ~2M tokens/day average, peaks ~5M tokens/day during campaigns.
- Key features in use: streaming responses, function/tool-calling, embeddings for search.
- Regs: PII in some flows, need audit logs and KMS integration for sensitive routes.

Success criteria for migration to open models
- Performance: maintain p95 latency <= 200ms for 512-token prompts (user-facing).
- Cost: target >= 40% reduction in model spend versus current baseline.
- Feature parity: support streaming and function-calling patterns with minimal prompt/template changes.
- Safety/quality: comparable hallucination/accuracy on your evaluation set.
- Ops: ability to rollout canary & fallback to current endpoints with traffic split.

Model shortlist we discussed
- Llama 3 (various sizes) - good general-purpose candidate
- Mistral / Mistral Large - strong open model family
- Falcon - lower-cost large context variants
- Vendor-hosted tuned variants (if you need fully managed)

Compatibility needs
- Tool/function-calling equivalence or adapter layer
- Streaming API with SSE/chunked responses
- Tokenization parity for existing embeddings/prompt templates or migration plan
- Key management integration (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for regulated routes

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) Technical deep-dive w/ infra & model ops (30-45m) - proposed Wed May 20, 10:00am PT - covers benchmarks, quantization options, and endpoint routing.
2) Redwood to provide: compatibility matrix & suggested model/quantization choices + preliminary cost estimate (I attached the compatibility matrix).
3) Shoply to provide: representative prompt set, 2-3 evaluation flows, and the evaluation dataset (redacted) for quality checks.
4) Trial: 2-week POC with canary routing + cost/sla measurements.

Attachments: Shoply_Migration_RFP.pdf (you shared) and redwood-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (attached).

If that looks right I'll send a calendar invite for Wed and loop Rishi for the kernel/quantization discussion.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Tom Hernandez <tom@shoply.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@shoply.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Marissa - thanks, this is a helpful summary and captures the conversation well. A few clarifications:

- Volume: the 2M tokens/day is a current steady-state; marketing promos have produced short-lived peaks up to ~6M tokens/day.
- Regulated data: most flows are PII, not PHI, but we need strict retention windows and auditability for audit teams.
- Function calling: Priya flagged that our current pipelines rely heavily on tool-calling (structured JSON responses). Any adapter needs to preserve that.

We're happy to do the trial on the proposed dates. Wed May 20 at 10:00am PT works for the technical deep-dive - Priya and our infra lead will join.

One ask: could you include an initial mapping of our current prompt templates to the adapter changes we might need (high-level)? That'll help Priya scope the work.

Thanks - looking forward to the deep-dive.

Tom Hernandez
Head of Product
Shoply
Tom.Hernandez@shoply.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hernandez <tom@shoply.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@shoply.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks - invite sent for Wed May 20, 10:00am PT (link: https://meet.redwood.ai/meet/83471). Rishi will join and bring our benchmark plan + quantization options.

I attached the compatibility matrix and a short mapping doc to outline common prompt adapter patterns we use (tokenization notes, function-call wrappers, streaming adapters). In the deep-dive we'll run through:
- Benchmarks (latency/cost at your steady and peak profiles)
- Quantization tradeoffs (FP16 / 4-bit / int8) and expected cost/latency impact
- Canary / routing strategies and rollback paths
- Data protection (KMS + audit logs) and what we'll need from your side

Mutual action plan (short):
- Redwood: deliver lightweight POC within 5 business days after the tech deep-dive (includes hosted endpoints and a cost baseline).
- Shoply: provide eval prompts and a redacted dataset, and access to an infra contact for routing/testing.

See you on Wed.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-compatibility-matrix.xlsx
